answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. If several identities controlled by one attacker coordinate to fake demand, they still need to fund every account; matching behavior can trigger an audit, and proof of common control can forfeit those stakes. This does not make Sybils impossible: it makes influence costly in proportion to identities and exposure. An oasis of honest agents can spot a plume of coordinated claims, while a wander account earns influence only by putting real capital at risk.
